To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) that can be used for the diagnosis of paraneoplastic autoimmune multiorgan and mucocutaneous (MOM) disease.

we have developed ELISAs that use recombinant proteins as the antigens and are highly sensitive and highly specific for the diagnosis for PNP, and that these ELISAs are useful tools for the diagnosis of paraneoplastic autoantibody diseases.

the expression of recombinant proteins in a human cell is an effective way to obtain highly sensitive and specific ELISA antigens for the detection of autoantibody against envoplakin, periplakin and desmoglein3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of autoantibody in patients with paraproteinemia and autoimmune bullous diseases by ELISA.
the development of a new method for detecting autoantibodies in patients with parameoplastic pemphigsus.
the development of a new diagnostic method for PNP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ELISAs for the detection of anti-envoplakian and anti-periplakian antibodies are useful in the diagnosis of Pemphigus.

the ELISA using the recombinantly expressed linker subdomains of periplakin and/or envoplakin as the antigen can be a useful diagnostic tool for the diagnosis of paraneoplastic autoimmune multiorgan disease.
the ELISA for envoplakin and/or periplakin linker subdomain proteins is highly sensitive and specific, and may be used as a diagnostic marker for PNP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ELISA using recombinant linker domain of periplakin and recombinant envoplakin is a sensitive and specific method for PNP diagnosis.
the recombinant protein containing linker subdomain of periplakin or envoplakin expressed in a cell line could be used as the ELISA antigens for the diagnosis of paraneoplastic penphigus.
we have successfully developed a new ELISA for the diagnosis of paraneoplastic autoimmune mucocutaneous disease (PN-AMCD).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the linker subdomain of envoplakin is a major target antigen of anti-envoplakins autoantibodies in paraneoplastic PNP.
the ELISA using the recombinants of linker subdomains of these two proteins is highly sensitive and specific, which can be used as a simple method for the diagnosis of paraneoplastic PNP.
ELISA using recombinant proteins as the antigens may be a promising approach for the detection of autoantibody specificities.
